description: This collection publishes integrated power grid models that span every voltage level, from the extra-high-voltage transmission grid down to low-voltage distribution, with a high share of renewable generation. It is maintained by the Department of Electrical Power Supply at the Institute of Electric Power Systems, Leibniz University Hannover, and was first published in 2020 by Marcel Sarstedt, Neelotpal Majumdar, Christoph Blaufuß and Lutz Hofmann. Its stated motive is that standard benchmark grids are synthetic, often outdated for renewable integration and heavily adapted without full documentation, so results cannot be compared or reproduced; the department therefore publishes the exact input data used in each of its studies. Resources include a data format description in English and German, an example multi-level grid as a MATLAB file, and study data sets on flexibility aggregation at TSO-DSO interconnections, reactive power dispatch with transformer tap settings, and high- and medium-voltage grid scenarios. Coverage is German research grid models across all voltage levels. Files are downloadable from the university research data repository under CC BY 3.0 at no cost, and resources are still being added (metadata updated March 2026). Caveats: grids are research models tied to specific studies, not operator records, and some descriptions are only in German. Simulation uses are power flow, optimal power flow and flexibility aggregation across transmission and distribution. Related records: data-hannover-grid-planning-program-datasets comes from the same department.
